explanation.summary: Emergency contraception decisions turn on three variables: time since intercourse, position in the cycle, and body weight. Oral methods act by delaying ovulation, so they fail if the luteinising hormone surge has already begun, and day 13 of a 28 day cycle is precisely the highest risk window. The copper intrauterine device works after fertilisation as well as before, which is why it retains its efficacy up to five days after intercourse or five days after the earliest estimated ovulation. Both oral agents lose efficacy at higher body weight, and the woman who also wants ongoing contraception gains twice from the device. Screening swabs are taken at insertion rather than waiting for results, since delaying insertion is the greater risk.
key_points: Copper device failure rate is under 1 per cent and is unaffected by body weight
Oral emergency contraception works by delaying ovulation and fails after the surge
Levonorgestrel efficacy falls above about 70 kg
Ulipristal is blunted by starting a progestogen within five days
The hormonal intrauterine device is not an emergency contraceptive
explanation.pearls: A copper intrauterine device can be inserted up to five days after the earliest estimated ovulation rather than five days after intercourse, which extends the window well past day five in a woman who presents late in her cycle.

options.rationale: Levonorgestrel efficacy falls with increasing body weight and is markedly reduced above about 70 kg, and it is also the least effective option this late after intercourse (Source: Family Planning Australia Emergency Contraception).

The copper device is the most effective emergency method with a failure rate under 1 per cent, its action is not reduced by body weight or by the delay to 68 hours, and it converts the visit into ongoing long-acting contraception (Source: Family Planning Australia Emergency Contraception; RANZCOG Long Acting Reversible Contraception).

Doubling the dose is sometimes offered when no better option exists, but the evidence that it restores efficacy is weak and it should not displace a method that works (Source: Family Planning Australia Emergency Contraception).

Ulipristal outperforms levonorgestrel near ovulation but its efficacy also falls at higher body weight, and starting a progestogen within five days blunts its action (Source: Family Planning Australia Emergency Contraception).

The hormonal device is excellent ongoing contraception, but it is the copper ion rather than the progestogen that provides the emergency effect, so it does not meet the immediate need (Source: RANZCOG Long Acting Reversible Contraception).

explanation.summary: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy is diagnosed by pruritus without a primary rash together with raised serum bile acids, and the transaminases are frequently raised as well. Timing of birth is now stratified by the peak bile acid concentration rather than treated as a single decision for all affected women, because the stillbirth excess is confined almost entirely to those with concentrations of 100 micromol per litre or more. Ursodeoxycholic acid improves maternal itch and biochemistry but has not been shown to reduce perinatal death, so it does not alter the timing decision. Preeclampsia and gestational diabetes are more common in these women and should be screened for, and the condition recurs in up to 90 per cent of subsequent pregnancies.
key_points: Diagnosis requires pruritus without a primary rash plus raised serum bile acids
Timing of birth is stratified by the peak bile acid concentration
Concentrations of 100 micromol per litre or more prompt birth at 35 to 36 weeks
Ursodeoxycholic acid relieves itch but does not reduce perinatal death
Cardiotocography does not predict the sudden stillbirth of this condition
explanation.pearls: The three Australian bands are birth around 40 weeks for bile acids under 40 micromol per litre, 38 to 39 weeks for 40 to 99 micromol per litre, and 35 to 36 weeks for 100 micromol per litre or more.

sources.label: Royal Women's Hospital Victoria Clinical Guidelines

options.rationale: Birth at 38 to 39 weeks is the recommendation for a peak bile acid concentration of 40 to 99 micromol per litre, and applying it to a higher concentration leaves several weeks of the steepest stillbirth risk unaddressed (Source: RANZCOG Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy).

Cardiotocography does not predict the sudden stillbirth associated with this condition, which is thought to follow an acute bile acid mediated arrhythmia rather than progressive placental failure (Source: RANZCOG Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy).

A peak bile acid concentration of 100 micromol per litre or more carries a stillbirth risk several fold above background from around 35 weeks, so planned birth at 35 to 36 weeks is offered after discussing prematurity against that risk (Source: RANZCOG Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy).

There is no indication for immediate delivery at 31 weeks with normal fetal growth and Dopplers, and caesarean section is not the required mode of birth in this condition (Source: RANZCOG Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy).

Birth at around 40 weeks is appropriate for mild disease with bile acids under 40 micromol per litre, and this woman sits in the highest risk band (Source: RANZCOG Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy).

explanation.summary: Antenatal corticosteroids reduce neonatal death, respiratory distress syndrome and intraventricular haemorrhage, with the greatest effect when birth occurs between 24 hours and seven days after the first dose. Many women who receive a course do not deliver in that window, which created the question of repeat dosing, answered in Australia by the ACTORDS trial showing that single repeat doses reduce respiratory morbidity without the growth restriction seen with weekly multiple courses. The eligibility rules are therefore tight: more than seven days since the last dose, gestation below 32 weeks and 6 days, and a genuine likelihood of birth within seven days. Corticosteroid decisions sit alongside two other time-critical interventions in threatened preterm labour, namely magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection below 30 weeks and intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis against group B streptococcus, and confusing their gestational thresholds is a common error.
key_points: Maximum benefit occurs between 24 hours and seven days after the first dose
A single repeat dose is used, not a repeated full course
Repeat dosing applies below 32 weeks and 6 days when birth is likely within seven days
Weekly multiple courses reduce birth weight and head circumference
Magnesium sulfate neuroprotection applies below 30 weeks in Australia
explanation.pearls: The Australian repeat dose is betamethasone 11.4 mg intramuscularly as a single dose, and it can be given more than once in a pregnancy provided each is separated by at least seven days and gestation remains below 32 weeks and 6 days.

options.rationale: The benefit of a course wanes after about seven days, and withholding a repeat dose forgoes a demonstrated reduction in respiratory distress syndrome and the need for oxygen (Source: RANZCOG Antenatal Corticosteroids).

Weekly repeat courses reduce birth weight and head circumference without additional respiratory benefit, which is why Australian practice limits repeats to single doses (Source: RANZCOG Antenatal Corticosteroids).

Magnesium sulfate for fetal neuroprotection is offered below 30 weeks of gestation in Australia, so at 31 weeks and 2 days it does not apply, and it would not substitute for corticosteroid in any case (Source: RANZCOG Magnesium Sulfate for Neuroprotection).

A single repeat dose is recommended when more than seven days have elapsed since the first course, gestation is below 32 weeks and 6 days, and preterm birth is likely within the next seven days, all of which apply here (Source: RANZCOG Antenatal Corticosteroids).

A full dexamethasone course is an alternative first course rather than a repeat regimen, and giving four further doses exceeds the exposure supported by the repeat dose evidence (Source: RANZCOG Antenatal Corticosteroids).

explanation.summary: Postpartum contraception is timed around two competing risks: venous thromboembolism, which is highest in the first three weeks after birth, and the return of ovulation, which can occur from day 21 in a woman who is not exclusively breastfeeding. Progestogen only methods carry no additional thrombotic risk and no clinically significant effect on lactation, so implants, progestogen only pills and injections can all be started immediately. Combined hormonal methods are deferred to six weeks in breastfeeding women and to at least three weeks, or six weeks if other thrombotic risk factors are present, in women who are not breastfeeding. Intrauterine devices have an insertion window immediately after birth and then a gap until four weeks, which is the practical detail most often forgotten in general practice.
key_points: Ovulation can return from day 21 postpartum in women not fully breastfeeding
Progestogen only methods can be started at any time after birth
Combined hormonal methods are deferred to six weeks while breastfeeding
Intrauterine devices are inserted within 48 hours or after four weeks
Lactational amenorrhoea requires all three of its conditions to be met
explanation.pearls: Interpregnancy intervals shorter than 18 months are associated with higher rates of preterm birth and small for gestational age infants, which is a concrete reason to provide effective contraception at the first postnatal contact rather than at the six week visit.

options.rationale: Combined hormonal contraception is not recommended before six weeks postpartum in a breastfeeding woman because of the thrombotic risk of the early puerperium and possible effects on milk volume (Source: Family Planning Australia Contraception Guidance; UK Medical Eligibility Criteria).

Lactational amenorrhoea is only about 98 per cent effective while all three conditions hold, namely full breastfeeding, amenorrhoea and an infant under six months, and it is an inadequate plan for a woman who states she must not conceive (Source: Family Planning Australia Contraception Guidance).

Intrauterine devices are inserted within 48 hours of birth or deferred until at least four weeks postpartum, because insertion between those points carries a higher perforation and expulsion risk (Source: Family Planning Australia Contraception Guidance).

Ovulation can return from about 21 days postpartum in a woman who is not fully breastfeeding, and this couple has already resumed sex, so deferring leaves an unprotected interval (Source: Family Planning Australia Contraception Guidance).

Progestogen only methods can be started at any time postpartum including during breastfeeding, and the implant meets her request for a highly effective method that does not depend on daily adherence (Source: Family Planning Australia Contraception Guidance; UK Medical Eligibility Criteria).

explanation.summary: Obstetric anal sphincter injury complicates around 3 per cent of vaginal births in Australia and around 6 per cent of first vaginal births, and the outcome depends heavily on recognition at the time. Classification is by depth: 3a is less than half the external sphincter thickness, 3b is more than half, 3c involves the internal sphincter as well, and a fourth degree tear breaches the anorectal mucosa. Every woman should have a systematic rectal examination after vaginal birth precisely because these tears are missed when only the perineum is inspected. Repair is followed by a single dose of broad spectrum antibiotic, a laxative regimen for ten days, physiotherapy referral and follow up at six to twelve weeks, with a discussion about mode of birth in a future pregnancy.
key_points: Perform a rectal examination after every vaginal birth to identify sphincter injury
3a involves less than half the external sphincter and 3b more than half
3c adds internal sphincter involvement and fourth degree breaches the anorectal mucosa
Repair sphincter injuries in theatre with regional or general anaesthesia
Follow repair with antibiotics, laxatives and physiotherapy referral
explanation.pearls: Prescribe a stool softener such as lactulose for ten days after sphincter repair and avoid constipating agents, because straining against a fresh repair is a recognised cause of breakdown and persisting incontinence.

sources.label: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears
Royal Women's Hospital Victoria Clinical Guidelines

options.rationale: Any disruption of the external anal sphincter is a third degree tear, and Australian practice is repair in an operating theatre with adequate regional or general anaesthesia, good lighting and assistance, together with a single dose of intravenous antibiotic (Source: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears).
source_refs: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears

options.rationale: Birth suite repair under local anaesthesia is appropriate for first and second degree tears, and using it for a sphincter injury gives inadequate muscle relaxation and poorer identification of the retracted sphincter ends (Source: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears).
source_refs: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears

options.rationale: Delaying repair of a sphincter injury leads to retraction and fibrosis of the muscle ends and substantially higher rates of persisting faecal incontinence (Source: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears).
source_refs: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears

options.rationale: Secondary sphincter repair is reserved for injuries missed at birth or for failed primary repair, and it has poorer functional results than immediate repair (Source: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears).
source_refs: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears

options.rationale: A defunctioning stoma is considered only for extensive fourth degree injury with gross contamination, and it has no place in a partial thickness external sphincter tear with intact anorectal mucosa (Source: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears).
source_refs: RANZCOG Third and Fourth Degree Perineal Tears

explanation.summary: The renewed National Cervical Screening Program uses primary human papillomavirus testing every five years from 25 to 74 years of age, with partial genotyping that separates types 16 and 18 from the other oncogenic types. Self collection has been available to every screening participant since 2022 and performs equivalently to clinician collection for detecting the virus, which matters because under screened women account for most cervical cancers in Australia. The limitation is that cytology cannot be run on a self collected vaginal sample, so the management pathway is driven by genotype alone. Types 16 or 18 go straight to colposcopy, while other oncogenic types on a self collected sample lead to a clinician collected sample for cytology, or direct colposcopy if that is not acceptable to the woman.
key_points: Types 16 or 18 detected on any sample means direct colposcopy referral
Other oncogenic types on self collection lead to a clinician collected sample for cytology
Self collection performs equivalently to clinician collection for virus detection
Screening runs five yearly from 25 to 74 years of age
Under screened women account for the majority of cervical cancers in Australia
explanation.pearls: Types 16 and 18 cause about 70 per cent of cervical cancers, which is why their detection bypasses cytology triage entirely and sends the woman straight to colposcopy even when she has no symptoms and a normal examination.

options.rationale: A twelve month repeat is the pathway for oncogenic types other than 16 and 18 with negative or low grade cytology, and applying it here would delay diagnosis of a possible high grade lesion (Source: National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).

Detection of types 16 or 18 on any sample, including a self collected one, requires direct referral for colposcopy regardless of cytology, because these genotypes account for around 70 per cent of cervical cancers (Source: National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).

Cytology does not change the destination when types 16 or 18 are found, and requiring a speculum examination first adds a barrier for a woman who chose self collection for good reason (Source: National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).

Routine recall follows a negative human papillomavirus result, and returning a woman with a high risk genotype to five yearly screening misses the group at greatest risk of invasive disease (Source: National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).
Ultrasound does not visualise the transformation zone and has no role in the assessment of an abnormal screening result (Source: National Cervical Screening Program Guidelines).

explanation.summary: Antiphospholipid syndrome is the only cause of recurrent miscarriage for which treatment reliably improves live birth rates, which is why it is sought in every recurrent miscarriage workup alongside parental karyotype, uterine imaging and thyroid and glycaemic assessment. Laboratory diagnosis requires lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin or anti beta 2 glycoprotein I antibodies persisting on two occasions at least 12 weeks apart, and lupus anticoagulant alone is sufficient if persistent. The obstetric clinical criteria are three or more consecutive losses before ten weeks, one or more losses of a morphologically normal fetus at or beyond ten weeks, or a birth before 34 weeks for severe preeclampsia or placental insufficiency. Combined aspirin and heparin raises live birth rates to around 70 to 80 per cent, and these pregnancies also need growth surveillance and preeclampsia vigilance in the second half.
key_points: Antibodies must persist on two occasions at least 12 weeks apart
Lupus anticoagulant alone is sufficient if persistently positive
Aspirin plus prophylactic heparin is the treatment for purely obstetric disease
Therapeutic dose heparin is reserved for prior thrombosis
Corticosteroids and immunoglobulin do not improve live birth rates
explanation.pearls: Start low dose aspirin before or at conception and add prophylactic enoxaparin once an intrauterine pregnancy with a fetal heart is confirmed on ultrasound, continuing the heparin until six weeks postpartum because thrombotic risk persists into the puerperium.

options.rationale: Aspirin alone is less effective than combined therapy in obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome, and the addition of heparin is what improves the live birth rate in this group (Source: RANZCOG Recurrent Miscarriage; Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular).
Corticosteroids do not improve live birth rates in obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome and increase gestational diabetes, hypertension and preterm birth (Source: RANZCOG Recurrent Miscarriage).

Persistent lupus anticoagulant with three consecutive losses before ten weeks meets the criteria for obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome, treated with low dose aspirin plus prophylactic low molecular weight heparin started once an intrauterine pregnancy is confirmed (Source: RANZCOG Recurrent Miscarriage; Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular).

Therapeutic dose anticoagulation is used when there has been a prior thrombotic event, and this woman has purely obstetric disease so the higher dose adds bleeding risk without benefit (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular).
Immunoglobulin has not been shown to improve live birth rates in this condition and is not funded for this indication in Australia (Source: RANZCOG Recurrent Miscarriage).

explanation.summary: Lichen sclerosus is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis with a peak incidence after menopause, and it is repeatedly misdiagnosed as thrush because itch is the dominant symptom. The diagnosis is usually clinical, resting on white atrophic skin in a figure of eight distribution around the vulva and anus with loss of architecture, notably resorption of the labia minora and burying of the clitoris. Around 4 to 5 per cent of untreated women develop vulval squamous cell carcinoma, and there is good evidence that adherent topical corticosteroid treatment reduces that risk as well as controlling symptoms. Treatment is lifelong with a maintenance regimen after the initial induction course, and any persistent ulcer, fissure or thickened plaque during follow up is an indication for biopsy.
key_points: Itch that has failed repeated antifungal treatment should prompt reassessment
The figure of eight distribution and architectural loss are diagnostic clues
Ultrapotent topical corticosteroid is first line and is used long term
Around 4 to 5 per cent of untreated women develop vulval squamous cell carcinoma
Biopsy any ulcer, fissure or thickened plaque that appears during follow up
explanation.pearls: The usual Australian induction regimen is clobetasol propionate 0.05 per cent ointment nightly for four weeks, alternate nights for four weeks, then twice weekly for four weeks, followed by lifelong maintenance titrated to symptoms and examination findings.

options.rationale: A further antifungal repeats a treatment that has already failed three times and does not address an inflammatory scarring dermatosis (Source: RANZCOG Vulval Skin Disorders).
Topical oestrogen treats genitourinary syndrome of menopause, but the vaginal walls are normal here while the changes are confined to keratinised vulval skin (Source: RANZCOG Vulval Skin Disorders).

Biopsy is required when the appearance is atypical, when there is an ulcer or thickened area, or when the condition fails to respond, and none of those apply to this classic presentation (Source: RANZCOG Vulval Skin Disorders).

An ultrapotent topical corticosteroid is first line for lichen sclerosus, relieving symptoms, halting architectural change and reducing the risk of vulval squamous cell carcinoma (Source: RANZCOG Vulval Skin Disorders; Australian Medicines Handbook).

Surgery has no role in uncomplicated lichen sclerosus, recurs in the surgical scar, and is reserved for malignancy or for division of adhesions causing functional problems after medical control (Source: RANZCOG Vulval Skin Disorders).

explanation.summary: Early onset group B streptococcal disease remains the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in the first week of life, and intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis reduces it by around 80 per cent when given for at least four hours before birth. Australian units use either universal screening with a combined vaginal and rectal swab at 35 to 37 weeks or a risk factor based approach, and both require a clear antibiotic algorithm. Benzylpenicillin is first line, cefazolin is used for non severe penicillin allergy, and severe immediate allergy leads to clindamycin if the isolate is susceptible or vancomycin if it is not, which is why susceptibility testing is requested on every antenatal isolate from a woman reporting penicillin allergy. Documenting the nature of the reaction matters as much as the label itself, since most reported penicillin allergies are not immunoglobulin E mediated and unnecessarily divert women to inferior agents.
key_points: Prophylaxis is most effective when given at least four hours before birth
Benzylpenicillin is first line and cefazolin covers non severe allergy
Severe immediate allergy requires clindamycin only if the isolate is susceptible
Vancomycin is used when the isolate is clindamycin resistant
Request susceptibility testing on antenatal isolates from penicillin allergic women
explanation.pearls: Ask specifically whether the penicillin reaction involved angioedema, breathing difficulty, hypotension or adrenaline, because that single question separates the women who can safely receive cefazolin from those who need vancomycin.

options.rationale: A cephalosporin is acceptable for a non severe penicillin allergy such as a delayed rash, but a history of angioedema with airway involvement requiring adrenaline is a severe immediate reaction where cross reactivity risk is unacceptable (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).
Clindamycin is the alternative for severe penicillin allergy only when the isolate is susceptible, and this isolate has been reported as resistant (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Macrolides achieve poor and unreliable concentrations in fetal tissues and this isolate is resistant, so erythromycin is no longer recommended for this indication (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Withholding prophylaxis in a colonised woman leaves a risk of early onset neonatal sepsis of around one in 200, and observation does not prevent the disease it is watching for (Source: RANZCOG Maternal Group B Streptococcus).

With a severe immediate penicillin allergy and an isolate resistant to clindamycin, vancomycin is the recommended agent for intrapartum group B streptococcal prophylaxis in Australia (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic; RANZCOG Maternal Group B Streptococcus).

explanation.summary: Placenta accreta spectrum is rising in incidence in step with the caesarean section rate, and the combination of a previous caesarean with an anterior placenta praevia is the highest risk situation in obstetrics. Antenatal diagnosis is what changes outcome, because planned birth in an appropriate centre halves major haemorrhage and intensive care admission compared with unexpected diagnosis at delivery. The ultrasound features to know are loss of the clear zone, placental lacunae with turbulent flow, bladder line interruption, myometrial thinning and increased subplacental vascularity, with magnetic resonance imaging reserved for posterior placentas or uncertain findings. Delivery is planned before labour begins, usually at 34 to 36 weeks after corticosteroids, with the whole team, cross matched blood and cell salvage available, and the placenta is left undisturbed while hysterectomy proceeds.
key_points: Previous caesarean with an anterior praevia is the highest risk combination
Loss of the clear zone, lacunae and bladder line interruption are the key ultrasound signs
Plan birth at 34 to 36 weeks before labour begins
Leave the placenta in situ rather than attempting removal
Deliver in a centre with interventional radiology and massive transfusion capacity
explanation.pearls: The risk of accreta spectrum in a woman with placenta praevia rises from about 3 per cent with no previous caesarean to over 40 per cent with two or more, which is why the number of previous caesareans is the first question asked when a praevia is reported.

sources.label: RANZCOG Placenta Praevia and Accreta Spectrum

options.rationale: These ultrasound features indicate placenta accreta spectrum, and Australian practice is planned birth at 34 to 36 weeks with the placenta left in situ and hysterectomy performed by a multidisciplinary team in a centre with interventional radiology, critical care and massive transfusion capability (Source: RANZCOG Placenta Accreta Spectrum).

Attempting to separate an abnormally invasive placenta is the single act most likely to cause catastrophic haemorrhage, and waiting to 39 weeks greatly increases the chance of an unplanned emergency birth (Source: RANZCOG Placenta Accreta Spectrum).

Labour is contraindicated with a placenta covering the internal os regardless of invasion, and praevia alone determines mode of birth while accreta spectrum determines timing and setting as well (Source: RANZCOG Placenta Praevia and Accreta Spectrum).
source_refs: RANZCOG Placenta Praevia and Accreta Spectrum

options.rationale: Prophylactic arterial occlusion is an adjunct used within a planned procedure rather than a substitute for planning the timing and place of birth, and its benefit remains unproven (Source: RANZCOG Placenta Accreta Spectrum).

Deferring the plan wastes the interval in which corticosteroids, blood product planning and transfer to an appropriate centre must be arranged, and around a third of these women bleed before their planned date (Source: RANZCOG Placenta Accreta Spectrum).

explanation.summary: Menopausal hormone therapy remains the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms, and the modern decision is less about whether to prescribe than about which route and which progestogen. Route matters because oral oestrogen increases hepatic production of clotting factors, roughly doubling venous thromboembolism risk, while transdermal delivery bypasses the liver and has not shown that association in observational data. Progestogen choice matters because micronised progesterone and dydrogesterone carry a lower breast cancer signal than synthetic progestogens, while providing adequate endometrial protection. A single provoked thrombosis with a negative thrombophilia screen and no ongoing risk factor does not preclude therapy, whereas unprovoked or recurrent events, or an inherited thrombophilia, warrant haematology input first. Obesity independently raises baseline thrombotic risk, which strengthens rather than removes the case for the transdermal route.
key_points: Transdermal oestradiol avoids the first pass hepatic effect on clotting factors
An intact uterus always requires a progestogen for endometrial protection
Micronised progesterone has the most favourable breast and thrombotic profile
A single provoked thrombosis is not an absolute contraindication
Obesity raises baseline thrombotic risk and favours the transdermal route
explanation.pearls: Transdermal oestradiol at doses of 50 micrograms per 24 hours or less has not been shown to increase venous thromboembolism risk even in women with a prior provoked event, which is the specific evidence that allows treatment in this situation.

options.rationale: Oral oestrogen undergoes first pass hepatic metabolism and raises the risk of venous thromboembolism, and medroxyprogesterone acetate carries a higher breast cancer and thrombotic signal than micronised progesterone (Source: Australasian Menopause Society).

Transdermal oestradiol avoids first pass metabolism and has not been associated with increased venous thromboembolism, and micronised progesterone provides the endometrial protection required by an intact uterus with the most favourable risk profile (Source: Australasian Menopause Society; Australian Medicines Handbook).
Unopposed oestrogen in a woman with an intact uterus causes endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma, and the oral route adds the thrombotic concern (Source: Australasian Menopause Society).

Tibolone is effective for vasomotor symptoms but is associated with an increased risk of stroke in older women and does not have the thrombotic safety data of transdermal oestradiol (Source: Australasian Menopause Society).

A previous provoked thrombosis with a negative thrombophilia screen is not a contraindication to transdermal therapy, and a non hormonal alternative gives roughly half the symptom reduction (Source: Australasian Menopause Society).

explanation.summary: Adnexal torsion is around five times more common in pregnancy than outside it, most often in the first and early second trimesters when an enlarged corpus luteum or a persistent cyst provides the lead point. Ultrasound findings of an enlarged oedematous ovary with peripherally displaced follicles and a twisted pedicle are more reliable than Doppler flow, because dual blood supply means arterial flow can persist in a torted ovary and its presence does not exclude the diagnosis. The historical practice of removing a blue or black ovary has been abandoned, since colour at operation reflects venous congestion rather than necrosis and the great majority of conserved ovaries regain follicular activity on later imaging. Malignancy risk in a torted ovary is low, and cystectomy at the same operation is often deferred to allow the oedema to settle. In pregnancy, laparoscopy is safe with open entry or a left upper quadrant approach and appropriate insufflation pressures.
key_points: Preserved Doppler arterial flow does not exclude ovarian torsion
Peripherally displaced follicles and a twisted pedicle are the key ultrasound signs
The colour of the ovary at surgery does not predict recovery of function
Detorsion with conservation is standard where fertility matters
Laparoscopy is safe in the second trimester with appropriate entry technique
explanation.pearls: Most conserved ovaries show normal follicular development on ultrasound within three to six months of detorsion, and the theoretical risk of thromboembolism from untwisting a congested pedicle has not been borne out in practice.

sources.label: Royal Women's Hospital Victoria Clinical Guidelines

options.rationale: Removing the ovary because it looks dark and oedematous is the classic error, since the appearance at surgery correlates poorly with viability and most untwisted ovaries recover function (Source: RANZCOG Adnexal Masses in Pregnancy).

Torsion is a surgical emergency in which every hour of delay increases the chance of irreversible infarction, and imaging in 24 hours will only document a dead ovary (Source: RANZCOG Adnexal Masses in Pregnancy).

Prompt laparoscopic untwisting with ovarian conservation is the standard approach at any age when future fertility matters, and laparoscopy is safe in the second trimester with appropriate port placement (Source: RANZCOG Adnexal Masses in Pregnancy).

Laparotomy is reserved for suspected malignancy, haemodynamic instability or where laparoscopic access is not feasible, and it combines an unnecessary open approach with unnecessary ovarian loss (Source: RANZCOG Adnexal Masses in Pregnancy).
The second trimester is the preferred window for non-urgent surgery in pregnancy, but this is an emergency where the timing rule does not apply (Source: RANZCOG Adnexal Masses in Pregnancy).

explanation.summary: Treatment of fibroid related heavy menstrual bleeding is decided by location far more than by size, which is why the FIGO classification numbers fibroids from 0 for wholly intracavitary through to 7 for pedunculated subserosal. Types 0, 1 and 2 are submucosal and are the ones most strongly associated with both heavy bleeding and impaired implantation, and types 0 and 1 are the ones removable hysteroscopically because less than half their volume sits in the myometrium. The presence of a reproductive intention changes the whole algorithm, ruling out hysterectomy, endometrial ablation and embolisation. The iron deficiency should be treated in parallel, since a ferritin of 8 micrograms per litre with microcytic anaemia will not correct without replacement even after the bleeding is controlled.
key_points: Fibroid location determines treatment more than fibroid size
FIGO types 0 and 1 are amenable to hysteroscopic resection
Submucosal fibroids impair implantation as well as causing heavy bleeding
Reproductive intention excludes ablation, embolisation and hysterectomy
Treat the iron deficiency in parallel with the structural problem
explanation.pearls: A FIGO type 2 fibroid has more than half its volume within the myometrium and is usually beyond safe hysteroscopic resection, so the proportion inside the cavity rather than the diameter decides whether a hysteroscopic approach is possible.

options.rationale: The intrauterine system is first line for heavy menstrual bleeding without cavity distortion, but it is contraceptive and expulsion rates are high when a submucosal fibroid distorts the cavity (Source: RANZCOG Heavy Menstrual Bleeding).

Embolisation is effective for bulk symptoms from intramural fibroids but is not recommended for women intending pregnancy because of effects on ovarian reserve and placentation (Source: RANZCOG Heavy Menstrual Bleeding).

Tranexamic acid reduces blood loss by around a third and is a useful holding measure, but it does not treat the cavity distortion that is contributing to both the bleeding and the difficulty conceiving (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

A submucosal fibroid with less than half its volume in the myometrium is amenable to hysteroscopic resection, which reduces menstrual loss and improves conception rates in a woman trying to become pregnant (Source: RANZCOG Heavy Menstrual Bleeding; RANZCOG Fibroids).

Hysterectomy is definitive for bleeding but ends fertility, which is unacceptable to a woman actively trying to conceive with an otherwise treatable single lesion (Source: RANZCOG Heavy Menstrual Bleeding).

explanation.summary: Hyperemesis gravidarum is defined by protracted vomiting with dehydration, electrolyte disturbance and weight loss of more than 5 per cent of booking weight, and it is distinguished from ordinary nausea and vomiting of pregnancy by those objective features rather than by symptom severity alone. Isotonic saline with potassium is the fluid of choice because these women are sodium and potassium depleted, while dextrose containing fluid can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy in a thiamine deplete patient and offers no advantage. A suppressed thyroid stimulating hormone with a high normal free thyroxine and no goitre or eye signs is gestational transient thyrotoxicosis driven by human chorionic gonadotrophin, which resolves as the pregnancy advances and does not need antithyroid treatment. Antiemetics are then given parenterally in a stepwise fashion, and thromboprophylaxis is considered because dehydration and immobility raise thrombotic risk.
key_points: Weight loss above 5 per cent with ketosis and electrolyte disturbance defines the condition
Isotonic saline with potassium is the fluid of choice, not dextrose
Give thiamine before or with any carbohydrate containing fluid
Transient gestational thyrotoxicosis needs no antithyroid treatment
Consider thromboprophylaxis during admission for dehydration
explanation.pearls: Thiamine 100 mg intravenously daily for three days is given to any pregnant woman who has vomited for more than three weeks before glucose containing fluid is started, because Wernicke encephalopathy in this setting typically presents with confusion and eye signs after rehydration rather than before it.

sources.label: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy

options.rationale: Glucose containing fluid given before thiamine can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy in a woman with prolonged vomiting, and dextrose alone does not replace the sodium and potassium she has lost (Source: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy).
source_refs: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy

options.rationale: Oral first line antiemetics are appropriate for milder disease, but a woman who has kept nothing down for 48 hours will not absorb them and needs parenteral treatment (Source: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy).
source_refs: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy

options.rationale: The same absorption problem applies, and this plan leaves a dehydrated hypokalaemic woman with a 7 per cent weight loss to manage at home (Source: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy).
source_refs: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy

options.rationale: Enteral feeding is considered only after intravenous rehydration and combination antiemetics have failed over several days, so it is not the initial step (Source: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy).
source_refs: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy

options.rationale: Isotonic saline with added potassium corrects the volume and electrolyte deficit, and thiamine is given before or with any carbohydrate load because vomiting beyond three weeks depletes stores and risks Wernicke encephalopathy (Source: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy; Australian Medicines Handbook).
source_refs: RANZCOG Nausea and Vomiting of Pregnancy

explanation.summary: Gestational trophoblastic disease is followed by serial human chorionic gonadotrophin because the marker is exquisitely sensitive and the whole surveillance system depends on being able to interpret its trajectory. Around 15 to 20 per cent of complete moles and one to five per cent of partial moles develop persistent trophoblastic neoplasia, which is diagnosed on a plateau across four values over three weeks, a rise across three values over two weeks, or persistent elevation beyond six months, rather than on symptoms. Surveillance duration in Australian practice depends on how quickly the marker normalises after evacuation, with a shorter period when normalisation is rapid. Persistent disease is highly curable with chemotherapy, and future pregnancies carry a modestly increased risk of a further molar pregnancy, so early ultrasound is arranged in any subsequent conception.
key_points: Reliable contraception is required throughout surveillance so the marker stays interpretable.
Hormonal contraception is safe and does not increase the risk of persistent disease.
An intrauterine device is deferred until the marker has normalised.
Persistent disease is diagnosed on a plateau or rise in serial values, not on a single result.
Early ultrasound is arranged in any subsequent pregnancy because of the recurrence risk.
explanation.pearls: A complete mole is diploid and entirely paternal in origin, most often from a single sperm duplicating within an empty ovum, which is why it produces no fetal tissue, higher marker concentrations and a substantially greater risk of persistent disease than the triploid partial mole.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: A single check cannot detect the plateau or rise that defines persistent trophoblastic disease, which is diagnosed on the shape of the curve across serial values rather than on any one number (Source: Cancer Council Australia).

Conception during surveillance destroys the interpretability of the marker and would either mask persistent disease or force an unnecessary termination to allow treatment (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: A second evacuation is considered for persistent bleeding or a plateauing marker with retained tissue on imaging, and her marker is falling steeply with an empty uterus, so re instrumentation adds adhesion and perforation risk for no gain (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Reliable contraception is essential because a new pregnancy makes the surveillance marker uninterpretable, hormonal methods are safe and do not increase the risk of persistent disease, and serial measurement continues until the concentration normalises and then for the defined surveillance period (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: An intrauterine device is avoided until the marker has normalised because insertion into a uterus that may still harbour trophoblastic tissue risks perforation and bleeding (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Varicella in pregnancy threatens both the mother, through pneumonia which is more severe than in the non pregnant state, and the fetus, through congenital varicella syndrome when infection occurs before 28 weeks and through neonatal varicella when it occurs around the time of birth. Congenital varicella syndrome is uncommon, affecting around one to two per cent of pregnancies with infection before 20 weeks, and causes limb hypoplasia, cutaneous scarring in a dermatomal distribution, eye defects and neurological damage. Post exposure prophylaxis with immunoglobulin reduces the likelihood and severity of maternal infection but does not eliminate fetal risk, so a woman who receives it still needs to report any rash promptly. The most important preventive step happens before pregnancy: checking varicella serology at preconception or postnatal visits and vaccinating non immune women.
key_points: Around 90 per cent of adults are immune despite an absent or uncertain history.
Immunoglobulin is given as soon as possible and up to ten days after first exposure.
Varicella vaccine is live attenuated and contraindicated during pregnancy.
Infection before 28 weeks risks congenital varicella syndrome; infection near birth risks neonatal varicella.
Antiviral treatment is started within 24 hours of any rash appearing.
explanation.pearls: Maternal rash appearing from seven days before to seven days after birth is the highest risk window for the newborn, and that infant receives immunoglobulin regardless of maternal treatment because there has been no time for protective maternal antibody to cross the placenta.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: This is a live attenuated vaccine and is contraindicated during pregnancy, and it is offered postpartum instead to non immune women before a subsequent pregnancy (Source: Australian Immunisation Handbook).

Antiviral treatment is started when a rash appears rather than as post exposure prophylaxis, and beginning it now would neither prevent infection nor be timed to the first 24 hours of the rash when it is most effective (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Waiting for a rash forfeits the prophylaxis window entirely, and maternal varicella pneumonia carries appreciable mortality while infection in this gestational range risks congenital varicella syndrome (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Around 90 per cent of adults are immune even without a recalled history, so urgent antibody testing avoids giving a scarce blood product unnecessarily, and immunoglobulin is effective when given as soon as possible and up to ten days after first exposure (Source: Australian Immunisation Handbook).

Giving it blind is defensible only when the result cannot be obtained inside the effective window, and here two days have elapsed with a ten day window and a same day assay available (Source: Australian Immunisation Handbook).

explanation.summary: Acute uterine inversion is rare, occurring in perhaps one in several thousand births, and is most often precipitated by cord traction on a fundally implanted placenta before the uterus has contracted. The clinical signature is the combination of sudden severe pain, cardiovascular collapse disproportionate to blood loss, an absent fundus on abdominal palpation and a mass at or through the cervix. Immediate manual replacement by pushing the part that inverted last back first, with the palm supporting the fundus, succeeds in the majority if performed before the constriction ring tightens. If it fails, hydrostatic replacement using warmed saline run into the vagina against a seal is the next step, and laparotomy with the Huntington or Haultain procedure follows. Uterotonics are withheld until the uterus is back in position and then given promptly, because atony immediately afterwards is common.
key_points: Shock out of proportion to blood loss with an absent fundus is the diagnostic combination.
Uterotonics are stopped before replacement and restarted immediately afterwards.
Manual replacement pushes back the part that inverted last, first.
Hydrostatic replacement follows failed manual replacement, then surgical correction.
The placenta is left attached if still adherent, because separating it first increases blood loss.
explanation.pearls: If manual replacement fails because the ring has already tightened, a tocolytic such as glyceryl trinitrate or terbutaline relaxes the cervical ring and frequently allows a second attempt to succeed without laparotomy.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
Royal Women's Hospital Victoria Clinical Guidelines

options.rationale: Surgical correction is reserved for failure of manual and hydrostatic replacement, and every minute of delay allows the ring to tighten and oedema to worsen, making bedside replacement less likely to succeed (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: A tamponade balloon has a role after the uterus has been replaced and bleeding continues, but inflating one inside an inverted uterus would drive the fundus further down (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: The degree of shock is out of proportion to the measured loss because traction on the peritoneal structures produces a profound vagal response, and the uterotonic must be stopped before replacement because a contracted uterus cannot be pushed back through the cervical ring (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Additional uterotonic tightens the constriction ring around the inverted fundus and converts a replaceable inversion into one requiring laparotomy (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Bimanual compression is the correct manoeuvre for atonic haemorrhage, but an atonic uterus is boggy and palpable abdominally rather than absent from its usual position (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Congenital syphilis is preventable and is diagnosed in Australia often enough to have prompted expanded screening in areas of high incidence, with repeat testing in the third trimester and at birth in addition to the booking screen. Vertical transmission is highest in primary and secondary disease, approaching 100 per cent, and falls with increasing duration of latent infection but never disappears. Benzathine penicillin is the only agent proven to treat the fetus, so a woman with a genuine penicillin allergy is desensitised and then treated with penicillin rather than given an alternative. Treatment more than 30 days before birth is required for the infant to be regarded as adequately treated in utero, and titres are followed to confirm at least a fourfold fall. Partner notification and treatment are essential, since reinfection during the remainder of the pregnancy would undo the benefit.
key_points: Benzathine penicillin is the only agent that reliably treats fetal infection.
Latent syphilis of unknown duration is treated with three weekly doses.
Genuine penicillin allergy is managed by desensitisation, not by substituting another class.
Treatment must be completed more than 30 days before birth for the infant to be considered treated.
Partner notification and treatment prevent reinfection later in the pregnancy.
explanation.pearls: The Jarisch Herxheimer reaction occurs within 24 hours in a substantial minority and can provoke uterine contractions and fetal heart rate abnormalities, so women treated after 20 weeks are advised to attend for monitoring if they develop fever, rigors or contractions after the injection.

sources.label: Australasian Society for HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Sexual Health Medicine

options.rationale: Macrolide resistance in Treponema pallidum is widespread and azithromycin crosses the placenta poorly, so it does not treat congenital infection (Source: Australasian Society for HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Sexual Health Medicine).
source_refs: Australasian Society for HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Sexual Health Medicine

options.rationale: Both treponemal assays are reactive with a titre of 1 in 32, which is not a pattern requiring confirmation, and a month of delay at 28 weeks materially raises the risk of congenital infection (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Seroconversion since an 11 week negative screen without any symptomatic stage means the duration cannot be established as under two years by history alone, and in pregnancy the safe course is the three dose weekly regimen, which also gives greater certainty of fetal treatment (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

One dose is the regimen for infection confidently established as early, and a single dose has a higher rate of fetal treatment failure, so it is not used when the stage is uncertain in pregnancy (Source: Australasian Society for HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Sexual Health Medicine).
source_refs: Australasian Society for HIV, Viral Hepatitis and Sexual Health Medicine

options.rationale: Doxycycline is the alternative for non pregnant patients with penicillin allergy, but tetracyclines are contraindicated in pregnancy and do not reliably treat the fetus (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

explanation.summary: Secondary amenorrhoea is worked through anatomically, from the hypothalamus down to the outflow tract, and the combination of normal gonadotrophins, normal oestradiol and a failed progestogen withdrawal points below the ovary. Intrauterine adhesions follow instrumentation of a recently pregnant uterus far more often than a non pregnant one, because the endometrial basal layer is thin and the myometrium soft, and puerperal curettage carries the highest risk of all. Cyclical pain without bleeding is a useful pointer because functioning endometrium is still responding but the blood cannot escape. Treatment is hysteroscopic division under direct vision, followed by measures to keep the cavity walls apart during healing, and outcomes for menstruation are good while fertility outcomes depend on the extent of the disease at the outset.
key_points: Normal gonadotrophins with normal oestradiol exclude ovarian and most central causes.
A failed progestogen withdrawal with adequate oestrogen localises the problem to the endometrium or outflow tract.
Instrumentation of a recently pregnant uterus is the dominant risk factor for adhesions.
Cyclical pain without bleeding suggests functioning endometrium behind an obstruction.
Hysteroscopy is both the diagnostic and the therapeutic procedure.
explanation.pearls: After adhesiolysis, a period of oestrogen therapy with or without a physical barrier keeps the raw cavity walls from re adhering, and a second look hysteroscopy at around two to three months is standard because recurrence rates reach a third in severe disease.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Normal gonadotrophins with an oestradiol in the follicular range show the ovary is working, and a failed progestogen withdrawal with cyclical pain after intrauterine instrumentation localises the problem to the outflow tract, where hysteroscopy both confirms adhesions and treats them (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Premature ovarian insufficiency is the tempting explanation for secondary amenorrhoea, but it produces a raised follicle stimulating hormone with a low oestradiol, and both of hers are normal (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Cross sectional imaging is insensitive for thin intrauterine adhesions and would not obviate hysteroscopy, which remains both the diagnostic and the therapeutic procedure (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Suppressing an endometrium that is already unable to shed treats nothing, and six months of delay allows adhesions to become denser and harder to divide (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Oestrogen priming corrects a hypo oestrogenic endometrium that is too thin to respond, but her oestradiol is already in the follicular range so priming would add nothing (Source: BMJ Best Practice: Amenorrhoea).

explanation.summary: Rhesus D alloimmunisation is prevented by giving anti-D immunoglobulin both routinely in the third trimester and after any potentially sensitising event. Sensitising events include abdominal trauma, antepartum haemorrhage, external cephalic version, invasive prenatal procedures, miscarriage and termination, and the dose depends on gestation: 250 IU up to 12 weeks and 625 IU thereafter. Routine antenatal prophylaxis in Australia is given as 625 IU at 28 and again at 34 weeks, and this is additional to rather than instead of event based doses. Quantification of feto maternal haemorrhage after events beyond 20 weeks determines whether the standard dose is adequate, since a large bleed requires further immunoglobulin calculated on the measured volume.
key_points: Anti-D is given within 72 hours of a sensitising event and remains worth giving if missed.
The dose is 250 IU up to 12 weeks and 625 IU after 12 weeks.
Quantification of feto maternal haemorrhage decides whether extra doses are needed.
Routine prophylaxis at 28 and 34 weeks is additional to event based doses.
Cord blood grouping after birth determines whether a postnatal dose is required.
explanation.pearls: Non-invasive fetal RhD genotyping on maternal plasma is now available in Australia and can spare an RhD negative woman carrying an RhD negative fetus from prophylaxis altogether, but where it is unavailable prophylaxis proceeds on the assumption that the fetus is RhD positive.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
National Blood Authority Guidelines on Prophylactic Use of Rh D Immunoglobulin

options.rationale: Abdominal trauma after 12 weeks is a sensitising event requiring 625 IU of anti-D as soon as possible and within 72 hours, with a quantification test sent at the same time to determine whether the bleed was large enough to need additional doses (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: The 250 IU dose is the correct one for sensitising events in the first trimester, and using it after 12 weeks under doses a pregnancy in which the fetal red cell volume is considerably larger (Source: National Blood Authority Guidelines on Prophylactic Use of Rh D Immunoglobulin).
source_refs: National Blood Authority Guidelines on Prophylactic Use of Rh D Immunoglobulin

options.rationale: The quantification test determines whether extra doses are needed, not whether the standard dose is given, and waiting for the result erodes the 72 hour window in which prophylaxis is effective (Source: National Blood Authority Guidelines on Prophylactic Use of Rh D Immunoglobulin).
source_refs: National Blood Authority Guidelines on Prophylactic Use of Rh D Immunoglobulin

options.rationale: Prophylaxis is given up to 72 hours after the event and is still worth giving beyond that if it has been missed, so an 18 hour delay is well inside the effective window (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: A repeat screen cannot be interpreted usefully at this point because passively acquired anti-D from prophylaxis is indistinguishable from immune anti-D on the screen, and delaying for the result serves no purpose (Source: National Blood Authority Guidelines on Prophylactic Use of Rh D Immunoglobulin).
source_refs: National Blood Authority Guidelines on Prophylactic Use of Rh D Immunoglobulin

explanation.summary: Endometrial hyperplasia is classified as with or without atypia, and that single distinction drives everything: hyperplasia without atypia has a progression risk under five per cent over 20 years and is treated with progestogen, while atypical hyperplasia carries a concurrent carcinoma rate of up to 40 per cent at hysterectomy and a high progression risk. Standard management of atypia is total hysterectomy, with the ovaries usually conserved in premenopausal women. Fertility sparing treatment is legitimate but is a specialist decision requiring imaging to exclude invasive disease, high dose progestogen and intensive sampling every three months until regression is confirmed twice, followed by prompt referral for assisted conception because relapse rates after treatment are high. Weight loss and treatment of insulin resistance are part of the plan, since unopposed oestrogen from peripheral aromatisation and anovulation is what generated the lesion.
key_points: Atypia carries up to a 40 per cent rate of concurrent carcinoma at hysterectomy.
Hysterectomy is standard once the family is complete; ovaries are usually conserved before menopause.
Fertility sparing treatment uses the intrauterine progestogen system with three monthly sampling.
Two consecutive negative biopsies are required before conception is attempted.
Weight loss and management of anovulation address the underlying oestrogen excess.
explanation.pearls: After successful regression on fertility sparing treatment, referral for assisted conception is made without delay because relapse occurs in around a quarter within two years, and hysterectomy is recommended once childbearing is complete.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Atypical hyperplasia progresses to carcinoma in a substantial proportion within a few years, so observation without treatment is not an option even when fertility is being preserved (Source: Cancer Council Australia).

For a woman who has not completed her family, high dose local progestogen delivered by intrauterine system achieves higher regression rates than oral progestogen and is combined with endometrial sampling every three months until two consecutive negative biopsies are obtained (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Hysterectomy is the standard treatment for atypical hyperplasia in a woman who has completed her family, but oophorectomy in a 42-year-old is not routine, and proceeding to surgery forecloses the pregnancy she is actively seeking (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Cyclical rather than continuous dosing is inadequate for atypical disease, and a twelve month surveillance interval is far too long when up to 40 per cent harbour a concurrent carcinoma (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Combined contraception provides insufficient progestogenic opposition for established atypia and carries additional risk at a body mass index of 38 kg/m2 (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

explanation.summary: Polycystic ovary syndrome is the commonest cause of anovulatory infertility and is diagnosed on two of three criteria: oligo or anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound, after excluding thyroid disease, hyperprolactinaemia and non classical congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Lifestyle intervention comes first because a loss of five to ten per cent of body weight restores ovulation in a substantial proportion, and it improves the response to every subsequent treatment. Where lifestyle alone does not restore ovulation, pharmacological induction proceeds in a defined order, and treatment is only started once tubal patency and semen analysis are known so that a couple is not put through cycles that cannot succeed. Cycle monitoring is required because these ovaries are exquisitely sensitive and multiple pregnancy is the main avoidable complication.
key_points: Diagnosis requires two of three criteria after exclusion of thyroid, prolactin and adrenal causes.
Weight loss of five to ten per cent restores ovulation in a meaningful proportion of women.
An aromatase inhibitor is first line for ovulation induction, ahead of the older oral agent.
Semen analysis and tubal patency are established before induction begins.
Follicle tracking limits multiple pregnancy in ovaries that are highly sensitive to stimulation.
explanation.pearls: Letrozole is given on cycle days two to six and works by transiently lowering oestrogen to release the pituitary from negative feedback, and because its half life is around 45 hours it has cleared well before implantation, which is why the early teratogenicity concern was not borne out.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

options.rationale: An aromatase inhibitor is first line for ovulation induction in this condition on the strength of higher live birth rates than the older agent, particularly in women with a raised body mass index, and cycles are monitored to limit multiple follicular development (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: The selective oestrogen receptor modulator was first line for decades and remains effective, but head to head trials show lower ovulation and live birth rates than the aromatase inhibitor, partly because its anti oestrogenic effect thins the endometrium and cervical mucus (Source: International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome).
source_refs: International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

options.rationale: Metformin improves menstrual regularity and metabolic parameters and can be added to ovulation induction, but as sole therapy it is inferior for achieving live birth (Source: International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome).
source_refs: International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

options.rationale: Assisted reproduction is third line in this setting, reserved for failure of oral agents and gonadotrophins or for a coexisting indication, and it carries a substantial risk of ovarian hyperstimulation in these women (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Gonadotrophins are second line after failure of an oral agent, and using them first exposes her to a higher multiple pregnancy and hyperstimulation risk with intensive monitoring that oral treatment avoids (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Secondary postpartum haemorrhage is bleeding from 24 hours to 12 weeks after birth, and the two dominant causes, retained products and endometritis, usually coexist because retained tissue provides the substrate for infection. Ultrasound has limited specificity in the puerperium since clot and normal involuting decidua can look identical to retained tissue, so vascularity on colour Doppler is the finding that most raises the likelihood of true retained products. The decision to operate balances the risk of continued bleeding against the risk of perforation and later intrauterine adhesions, both of which are considerably higher in a soft infected postpartum uterus. Where the bleeding is settling and the woman is stable, antibiotics alone allow many cases to resolve without instrumentation.
key_points: Secondary postpartum haemorrhage spans 24 hours to 12 weeks after birth.
Retained products and endometritis usually coexist and are treated together.
Colour Doppler vascularity raises the likelihood that echogenic material is retained tissue rather than clot.
Antibiotics are started before instrumentation to avoid precipitating bacteraemia.
Evacuation of an infected soft uterus is performed by an experienced operator because of perforation risk.
explanation.pearls: Intrauterine adhesions follow puerperal curettage in up to a fifth of cases, far more than after a non pregnant procedure, which is why gentle suction with the largest safe cannula under ultrasound guidance is preferred to sharp curettage.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Expectant management is reasonable for retained tissue found incidentally in a well woman with light loss, not for this presentation with sepsis and heavy ongoing bleeding (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Retained products with endometritis need broad spectrum intravenous cover started immediately, and because the bleeding is heavy and continuing, evacuation follows rather than waiting, performed by an experienced operator because the infected postpartum uterus perforates easily (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Instrumenting an infected uterus without antibiotic cover risks bacteraemia and septic shock, so the first dose goes in before the patient goes to theatre (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Oral therapy at home is appropriate for mild endometritis in a woman who is afebrile and not bleeding heavily, and she is tachycardic, febrile, rigoring and anaemic (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

A uterotonic may reduce loss transiently but does not clear retained tissue or treat the infection driving it, and a week of delay in a woman already at 92 g/L is unsafe (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Emergency contraception has three options in Australia and they differ in mechanism, window and reliability. The two oral agents work by delaying or preventing ovulation, which means both fail if the luteinising hormone surge has already begun, and both lose efficacy as body weight rises. The copper intrauterine device works by a direct toxic effect on gametes and by preventing implantation, so it is unaffected by weight and by where the woman is in her cycle, and it is more than ten times more effective than either oral agent. A pending sexually transmitted infection result does not delay insertion; the device is inserted and treatment is given if the result returns positive. Any woman offered emergency contraception should also leave with a plan for ongoing contraception, since the encounter is often the only opportunity.
key_points: The copper device is effective up to five days after intercourse and is unaffected by body weight.
Oral levonorgestrel is licensed to 96 hours; ulipristal to 120 hours.
Both oral agents lose efficacy at higher body mass index and fail after the luteinising hormone surge.
A pending infection screen does not delay device insertion.
Every emergency contraception consultation includes a plan for ongoing contraception.
explanation.pearls: Ulipristal is a progesterone receptor modulator, so starting a progestogen containing method within five days after it blunts its effect, and hormonal contraception is deferred for that interval with condoms used in the meantime.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Doubling the dose is sometimes used at higher body weight, but the supporting evidence is weak and the underlying limitation, that it only works if given before the luteinising hormone surge, still applies on day 12 (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Four days is still inside the window for a copper device, so declaring the opportunity closed would deny her the most effective option available (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: The copper device can be inserted up to five days after intercourse or up to five days after the earliest calculated ovulation, has a failure rate below one per cent that is unaffected by body weight, and simultaneously provides the ongoing contraception she has asked for (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: This agent is licensed to 120 hours and is the better of the two oral options, but its efficacy falls as body mass index rises above 30 kg/m2 and it remains substantially less effective than the device (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Oral levonorgestrel is licensed only to 96 hours and its efficacy declines markedly above a body mass index of 26 kg/m2, so both timing and body weight work against it here (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

explanation.summary: Twin to twin transfusion syndrome complicates around 10 to 15 per cent of monochorionic pregnancies and arises from unbalanced arteriovenous anastomoses within a shared placenta, which is why chorionicity determined in the first trimester dictates the entire surveillance schedule. Diagnosis requires a deepest vertical pocket below 2 cm in one sac with above 8 cm in the other before 20 weeks, using 10 cm as the upper threshold after 20 weeks, and discordant growth alone is not sufficient. Staging runs from isolated fluid discordance, through loss of the donor bladder, abnormal Dopplers, hydrops, to demise of either twin. Fetoscopic laser ablation is the definitive treatment because it addresses the anastomoses themselves, and outcomes are best when it is performed in a high volume centre, which is why monochorionic pregnancies are scanned fortnightly from 16 weeks so that referral happens early.
key_points: Chorionicity is established in the first trimester and drives the surveillance schedule.
Fortnightly ultrasound from 16 weeks is standard in monochorionic pregnancies.
Diagnosis requires deepest vertical pockets below 2 cm and above 8 cm before 20 weeks.
Loss of the donor bladder marks progression beyond the earliest stage.
Fetoscopic laser ablation treats the underlying anastomoses and outperforms amnioreduction.
explanation.pearls: Selective fetal growth restriction is the main differential and shows discordant estimated weights with normal amniotic fluid volumes, whereas this condition is defined by the fluid discordance and may occur with barely discordant weights.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines

options.rationale: Amnioreduction relieves maternal discomfort and pressure but leaves the shared placental anastomoses intact, and randomised comparison showed laser to give superior survival and less neurological morbidity (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Expectant surveillance is reasonable only for isolated discordant growth or for the mildest stage in selected cases, and untreated disease at this stage carries a perinatal mortality above 80 per cent (Source: International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines).
source_refs: International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines

options.rationale: Birth is not a treatment option at 19 weeks and steroids are given for anticipated preterm birth from 23 weeks, so this plan neither treats the condition nor is deliverable now (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.rationale: Deliberately perforating the dividing membrane equalises fluid volumes but creates a functionally monoamniotic pregnancy with cord entanglement risk and does not treat the vascular cause (Source: International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines).
source_refs: International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines

options.rationale: A deepest vertical pocket below 2 cm in one sac with above 8 cm in the other before 20 weeks defines the syndrome, and once the donor bladder is no longer visible the disease has advanced beyond the earliest stage, at which point fetoscopic laser ablation of the placental anastomoses gives the best survival (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Hyperthyroidism in early pregnancy has two dominant causes that need opposite management. Transient gestational thyrotoxicosis reflects cross stimulation of the thyroid stimulating hormone receptor by human chorionic gonadotrophin, peaks around 10 weeks, is associated with hyperemesis and resolves spontaneously without antithyroid drugs. Autoimmune disease persists, has a goitre, sometimes eye signs, and a positive receptor antibody, and it requires treatment because untreated maternal thyrotoxicosis increases miscarriage, pre eclampsia, preterm birth, fetal growth restriction and heart failure. The antithyroid drug is titrated to keep free thyroxine in the upper part of the non pregnant reference range using the smallest possible dose, because both agents cross the placenta and can cause fetal hypothyroidism and goitre if the mother is over treated.
key_points: Propylthiouracil is preferred in the first trimester; carbimazole is preferred thereafter and outside pregnancy.
Radioiodine is absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy and for six months before conception.
